previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease and prior CABG was admitted for left tricep and forearm pain, which she recognized as her anginal equivalent. She presented on the anniversary of her mother’s death and reported heightened anxiety. Initial evaluation showed normal cardiac enzymes and a normal chest X-ray. A stress test was non-diagnostic, with no ischemic changes, though nuclear imaging showed possible artifact-related perfusion irregularities. Cardiac catheterization revealed a 90% stenosis in the left circumflex artery, which was treated with percutaneous balloon angioplasty without stenting. The patient remained stable post-procedure, with resolution of symptoms. She was discharged home with increased metoprolol dose and aspirin 325 mg daily, with follow-up planned. Her arm pain after the procedure was brief and not deemed ischemic.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
